olivia-support: @raj heads-up — customer 'DataBright' started hitting 503s from hosted inference ~09:10 UTC. CS reports retries plus billing spikes. Logs show upstream worker restarts and a couple of segfaults. 

olivia-support: sample from gateway trace: `503 upstream worker error` then `x-request-id: ab12cd`. They said errors spike during large-batch requests (~max context) and when auth token refreshes.

raj-sre: thanks. any repro payloads or timestamps? can you paste last 5 min of runner logs?

olivia-support: pasted logs to incident channel but copying short excerpt: ```
[2026-03-17T09:10:12Z] infer-runner[pid=4217]: segfault at 0 ip=0x7f9f1a2d libattn.so...
[2026-03-17T09:10:12Z] kernel: Out-of-memory: Kill process 4217 (infer-runner) total-vm:820000k
[2026-03-17T09:10:13Z] orchestrator: container restart infer-runner-xyz status=OOM_RESTART
```

olivia-support: CS also saw `401` for ~30s overlapping the 503 window (customer token refresh happened), billing reported several thousand failed requests billed. Customer extremely upset.

jen-cs: I'm on a call with them in 10m. can we confirm if fallback routing kicked in? need to tell them what's being done.

mia-runtime: looks like two things intersected: large batch -> KV prefetch bumping GPU memory, plus token refresh causing sudden request bursts that hit the same pod. runtime didn't gracefully reject, worker OOMed then segfaulted. I'm checking if this model's quantization profile changed in last deploy.

raj-sre: good hypothesis. @deploy-bot do we have recent model swap or rollout around 09:00-09:08 UTC for that pool?

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] 2026-03-17T08:58:42Z model-swap: model-id=redwood-3b-quantized -> redwood-3b-q4_0 pipeline=hosted-eu-west pool=hb-gpu-14

raj-sre: bingo — a quantized swap at 08:58 could alter memory profile. mia, can you compare previous vs q4_0 mem calc? also check KV prefetch policy for that pool.

mia-runtime: running mem-delta now. early numbers show q4_0 uses approx +22% transient GPU VRAM on hot prefix prefetch corner cases. also seeing no per-request mem cap; we should enforce soft OOM guard.

aaron-oncall: immediate mitigation: 1) throttle request concurrency for that pool via routing (set max_concurrency=6), 2) apply emergency rollback to previous model version (if safe), 3) enable fallback routing to larger-pool (cpu-backed) for auth-failed requests so they don't pile on same GPUs. I can push routing throttles now.

raj-sre: do it. Jen, tell customer we are throttling their requests and routing failures to a fallback while we investigate; apologetic but reduces billing spam.

jen-cs: on call now. will update. also request credit for failed tokens — can finance review?

olivia-support: doing a quick repro with their payload (batch size 48, context ~12k tokens). reproduces OOM locally with q4_0 but not with previous float16. attaching short command: ```
python reproduce.py --model redwood-3b-q4_0 --batch 48 --context 12000 --profile mem
```

mia-runtime: thanks. I'll open a rollback PR for the pool and add a guard for request-level KV prefetch size. plan: rollback + throttle now, then schedule quant profile tuning.

aaron-oncall: throttles applied at 09:12 UTC and rollback initiated (status: in-progress). fallback routing enabled for 401/5xx at 09:14 UTC.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] 2026-03-17T09:12:05Z throttle-update applied pool=hb-gpu-14 max_concurrency=6

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] 2026-03-17T09:13:21Z rollout-rollback started model-id=redwood-3b-quantized -> redwood-3b-fp16 pool=hb-gpu-14

jen-cs: Customer briefed: we applied throttles and routing fallback, rollback in progress, they asked for credits. they're calmer but want root cause and a timeline. call ended.

raj-sre: next steps: (1) confirm rollback completes cleanly and monitors for further segfaults, (2) compute billing credit estimator for failed requests and pass to finance, (3) postmortem with action items: quant mem profiling gating, per-request soft OOM guard, routing policy to isolate auth-refresh storms.

olivia-support: noted. I'll create the incident ticket with reproducer and attach logs + timestamps. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
